synopsis: The glossary places cross-entropy methods in the booklet’s rare-event methods family; Chapter 9 describes these methods as deliberately oversampling dangerous conditions while estimating naturalistic rates through distribution-ratio reweighting [f14161, f6846]. Chapter 9 recommends cross-entropy, importance sampling and accelerated evaluation for small-probability estimation, with unbiased rates conditional on a known likelihood ratio and proposal coverage of the failure region [f7261, f7262]. Trustworthy rate estimation is not established when the naturalistic distribution is poorly known, and these methods carry high model dependence and potentially huge weight variance [f7264, f7265, f7266]. They cannot establish high-dimensional robustness or account for unmodelled physics; moreover, the independent evidence is marked as on-road, leaving an applicability gap for this heavy off-road program [f7263, f7268]. Typical tooling is in-house or academic [f7267].
